cases.id: set adds a key into an existing section
set adds the first key into an empty existing section
cases.note: An empty section is a childless block mapping whose span is its name token, not the whole file as the root's is: the root-vs-section split in the engine's block insert.

cases.id: set does not create a missing section
cases.note: INI has no literal for an empty nested mapping (`{}` is a two-character string), so `set` cannot start a section. Refused cleanly: no stray line is spliced in.

cases.id: appendValue and setSequence cannot start a list
cases.note: INI has no list, so nothing to start one with.

cases.id: deleteKey refuses a whole [section], and still deletes a key within it
cases.note: Zig error CannotDeleteSection. The section's span is its header's name token; deleteContainer is the op for a section.

cases.id: deleteKey on a repeated key takes every spelling
cases.note: A repeated key reads as one entry, its value the last spelling's. A delete that took only the first left the key reading on with the next spelling's value (`spelledAgain` in editor.zig).

cases.id: deleteKey on a key repeated across a reopened section leaves the reopening, empty
renameKey on a repeated key renames every spelling
cases.note: Afterwards s.z reads 4 and s.a is gone.

cases.id: replaceValue refuses a whole [section], and still replaces a value within it
cases.note: Zig error CannotReplaceSection. The section's span is the name token inside the header, so the generic splice used to write `[REPLACED]` and report success, renaming the section while its entries stayed under it.

cases.id: replaceValue at the root rewrites the whole document
cases.note: The root's span is the whole file: the one container the section guard exempts, and the reason the guard tests the path rather than sniffing for a `[`, which this source's first line would trip. Raw text, as the Zig test passed it: INI's value serializer cannot write a nested mapping (replaceValue with one is refused as UnsupportedFormat).

cases.id: deleteContainer removes a whole section
deleteContainer removes every occurrence of a reopened section
cases.note: `[a]` is scattered, and its second header is in no node's span. Without the parser's recorded header regions the trailing `[a]` would survive and adopt whatever followed it.

cases.id: deleteContainer takes every spelling of a key the section repeats
cases.note: The gather finds an entry's line through its span, which is the first spelling's; the other spelling used to stay and join the section before it once the headers went.

cases.id: deleteContainer takes a key repeated after a comment within one section
deleteContainer removes an empty reopened header too
cases.note: A reopen with no entries under it has nothing to find it by except the recorded header line: a gather that scanned upward from each child would leave it behind.

cases.id: deleteContainer takes owned comments with the section

cases.id: deleteContainer refuses a root-level scalar key
moveContainer relocates a section before another, collapsing its fragments
cases.note: `a`'s two fragments are removed and written again as one block at `b`. No blank line before it: the relocated block lands at the very start, with nothing before it to separate from.

cases.id: moveContainer with a null destination moves to the end
reorderContainers reorders named sections, leaving others in place
cases.note: `b` is untouched; `c` and `a` swap into the slot `a` held.

cases.id: set in a reopened section appends after its last physical entry
cases.note: A reopened section's entries thread onto the tail of one logical child list in file order, so the insert lands after the section's last occurrence with no multi-region gather, unlike TOML's scattered tables.

cases.id: moveKey refuses to move a [section], or to move an entry before one
cases.note: Zig error CannotMoveSection. Moving the section relocates its header alone, leaving `y = 2` for whichever section ends up above it; and "before `[b]`" is the tail of `[a]`'s body, so the root key `z` would have become `a.z`.

cases.id: moveKey still moves plain entries inside a section
reorderKeys refuses a reorder that shifts a section
cases.note:
Zig error CannotReorderSections. Used to write `z = 0
[a]
[b]
y = 2
x = 1
`: `[a]` emptied and `x = 1` rehomed into `b`.

cases.id: reorderKeys still reorders entries within a section
